blocks.text: `class FeeOrder(Order):` inherits from Order. An override replaces the inherited method for ordinary lookup on FeeOrder instances.
Inside an ordinary derived instance method, `super().method(arguments)` delegates lookup to the next class in method resolution order, not unconditionally to a fixed named parent.
In the derived initializer, use `super().__init__(quantity)` to run inherited initialization before adding the derived fee state where required.

segments.label: Extend inherited initialization with super().__init__()
segments.summary: A Developer needs the first name, last name and pay accepted by Employee, plus a programming language. Its own __init__ delegates the shared arguments through super().__init__ rather than duplicating Employee's initialization logic, then stores the programming language. Creating a Developer and displaying its email and programming language confirms that both inherited and derived initialization ran. In this single-base example, the delegated initialization is Employee's implementation.

bridge.before: Watch how Developer delegates shared initialization before storing its additional value. The clip calls Employee the parent; Devspace describes super() more precisely as lookup delegation to the next class in method resolution order. The claim that super() is necessary for multiple inheritance is too strong: it supports cooperative delegation but is not mandatory.
bridge.after: The clip demonstrates inherited initialization, but does not teach ordinary method overriding or next-class lookup semantics. The text covers both, using FeeOrder.cost() to extend inherited behavior.

exec('import pathlib

import shutil

import contextlib

import io

import json

import csv

import builtins

import ast


def super_probe(code):
    tree = ast.parse(code)
    for node in list(tree.body):
        if isinstance(node, ast.Expr) and isinstance(node.value, ast.Call) and isinstance(node.value.func, ast.Name) and node.value.func.id == "exec" and isinstance(node.value.args[0], ast.Constant):
            tree.body.extend(ast.parse(node.value.args[0].value).body)
    cls = next(n for n in ast.walk(tree) if isinstance(n, ast.ClassDef) and n.name == "FeeOrder")
    methods = {n.name: n for n in cls.body if isinstance(n, ast.FunctionDef)}
    init_call = ast.parse("super().__init__(quantity)").body[0]
    fee_store = ast.parse("self.fee = fee").body[0]
    format_return = ast.parse('return super().format() + f", fee: {self.fee}"').body[0]
    body = [ast.dump(n) for n in methods["__init__"].body]
    uses_init = ast.dump(init_call) in body and ast.dump(fee_store) in body and body.index(ast.dump(init_call)) < body.index(ast.dump(fee_store))
    uses_format = any(ast.dump(n) == ast.dump(format_return) for n in methods["format"].body)
    return any(isinstance(n, ast.Name) and n.id == "Order" for n in cls.bases) and uses_init and uses_format

def prepare_case(inputs):
    return inputs

def check_case(inputs):
    prepared = prepare_case(inputs)
    ns = dict(globals())
    ns.update(inputs)
    ns.update(prepared or {})
    source_code = pathlib.Path("main.py").read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    code = source_code.split("# BEGIN " + "LEARNER\n", 1)[1].split("# END " + "LEARNER", 1)[0]
    captured = io.StringIO()
    with contextlib.redirect_stdout(captured):
        exec(code, ns)
    return [ns["order"].quantity, ns["order"].fee, ns["order"].format(), captured.getvalue().strip(), super_probe(code)]
')

inputs = {'quantity': 3, 'fee': 2}
globals().update(inputs)
globals().update(prepare_case(inputs) or {})

# BEGIN LEARNER
class Order:

    def __init__(self, quantity):
        self.quantity = quantity

    def format(self):
        return f'Quantity: {self.quantity}'

# Define FeeOrder, its initializer, and its format override here.

import ast

        if isinstance(node, ast.Expr) and isinstance(node.value, ast.Call) and isinstance(node.value.func, ast.Name) and node.value.func.id == "exec" and isinstance(node.value.args[0], ast.Constant):
            tree.body.extend(ast.parse(node.value.args[0].value).body)
    cls = next(n for n in ast.walk(tree) if isinstance(n, ast.ClassDef) and n.name == "FeeOrder")

    body = [ast.dump(n) for n in methods["__init__"].body]
    uses_init = ast.dump(init_call) in body and ast.dump(fee_store) in body and body.index(ast.dump(init_call)) < body.index(ast.dump(fee_store))
    uses_format = any(ast.dump(n) == ast.dump(format_return) for n in methods["format"].body)

    ns = dict(globals())
    ns.update(inputs)
    ns.update(prepared or {})

inputs = {'quantity': 3, 'fee': 2}
globals().update(inputs)
globals().update(prepare_case(inputs) or {})

class Order:

    def __init__(self, quantity):

    def format(self):
